subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw enforce automatic sensitive-value sanitization on final agent outputs in core, route it to a plugin using existing outbound hooks, or keep core limited to the current log/tool/transcript redaction boundaries?
rationale: Source inspection proves a gap, but the requested behavior defines a security boundary and user-visible config policy that can change final replies, tool outputs, channel delivery, and false-positive behavior.

options.title: Approve a narrow core security design
options.body: Define an opt-in or explicitly scoped core sanitizer with schema, docs, tests, reporting, and delivery-surface coverage before implementation.

options.title: Route to plugin/ClawHub
options.body: Treat this as optional output policy implemented by a code plugin using `reply_payload_sending` and `message_sending`, and only add core SDK seams if the plugin proves a missing API.

options.title: Keep current redaction boundary
options.body: Document logs, transcripts, tool payloads, diagnostics, and UI safety surfaces as the supported core boundary and close or split final-output sanitization requests only after that maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core security design
recommendation.body: Define an opt-in or explicitly scoped core sanitizer with schema, docs, tests, reporting, and delivery-surface coverage before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision defines a sensitive-output security boundary and intersects CODEOWNERS security/config/secrets ownership.
